topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
summary: This topic covers modern lightweight and empirical software engineering methodologies designed for volatility, rapid value delivery, and continuous adaptation. It explores the Agile Manifesto and its four core value pairs, contrasting adaptive methods with heavy plan-driven models. The Scrum framework is thoroughly analyzed across its roles (Product Owner, Scrum Master, Cross-functional Dev Team), artifacts (Product Backlog, Sprint Backlog, Burndown Chart), and events (Sprint Planning, 15-minute Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective). Extreme Programming (XP) practices — notably Pair Programming (driver/navigator dynamics for knowledge spreading and collective ownership), Test-Driven Development (Red-Green-Refactor), Continuous Integration (CI), and Small Releases — are scrutinized. The topic also covers Kanban flow and Work-in-Progress (WIP) constraints, modern DevOps culture (automating the deployment pipeline with CI/CD and Infrastructure as Code), and open-source collaborative business models based on selling enterprise support and services.

key_terms.definition: A 2001 declaration of four core values prioritizing individuals/interactions, working software, customer collaboration, and responding to change over rigid plans.
The Scrum role responsible for maximizing product value, owning and prioritizing the Product Backlog, and acting as the customer's direct representative.
A servant-leader who coaches the team in agile practices, facilitates Scrum ceremonies, and actively removes organizational impediments and blockers.
A consistent, timeboxed iteration (typically 1 to 4 weeks) during which the Scrum team builds and delivers a potentially releasable product increment.
A 15-minute daily standup meeting for the development team to synchronize activities, report progress toward the Sprint Goal, and flag impediments.
An XP engineering practice where two developers work at one workstation (one Driver typing code, one Navigator reviewing and strategizing) to spread knowledge and reduce defect density.
A development discipline where unit tests are written before functional code in a rapid cycle: write failing test (Red), make it pass (Green), and optimize structure (Refactor).
The practice of automatically merging, building, and testing code changes from all developers into a shared mainline repository multiple times a day.
A constraint used in Kanban systems restricting the maximum number of task items allowed in any active workflow state to prevent bottlenecks.
A set of cultural philosophies, practices, and automated tools that integrates software development (Dev) and IT operations (Ops) for rapid, reliable delivery.

questions.topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
questions.question: In Nile University Final Exam Questions 9 & 53: What is a core fundamental principle of Agile software development?
options: Delivering working software quickly and frequently
Rigid adherence to initial project plans
Prioritizing extensive documentation over human interaction
Avoiding direct customer collaboration to prevent scope changes
questions.answer: Delivering working software quickly and frequently
questions.explanation: As tested in Nile Exam Q9 and Q53: Principle #3 of the Agile Manifesto states: 'Deliver working software frequently, from a couple of weeks to a couple of months, with a preference to the shorter timescale.' Working software is the primary measure of project progress.

why_wrong.Rigid adherence to initial project plans: Agile explicitly values 'responding to change over following a plan.'
Agile values 'working software over comprehensive documentation.'
Agile values 'customer collaboration over contract negotiation.'

marking_points: Identifies rapid, frequent delivery of working software as primary measure of progress
questions.source: Nile University Final Exam Paper (Type B), Questions 9 & 53

questions.topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
questions.question: In Nile University Final Exam Question 54: What is the primary purpose and advantage of Pair Programming in Extreme Programming (XP)?
options: Spread system knowledge and encourage collective code ownership
Halve the total salary paid to developers
Completely eliminate the need for automated unit testing
Allow one developer to sleep while the other writes code
questions.answer: Spread system knowledge and encourage collective code ownership
questions.explanation: In Pair Programming, the Driver writes code while the Navigator continuously reviews logic, checks syntax, and considers edge cases. This continuous peer review catches bugs immediately, breaks knowledge silos across the team, and establishes collective code ownership.

why_wrong.Halve the total salary paid to developer: Two developers working together on one task increases short-term labor cost slightly in exchange for vastly higher code quality.
why_wrong.Completely eliminate the need for automa: XP mandates Test-Driven Development (TDD) regardless of pair programming.
Both developers are actively, intellectually engaged in continuous collaboration.

marking_points: Encourages collective code ownership and continuous real-time review
questions.source: Nile University Final Exam Paper (Type B), Question 54

questions.topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
questions.question: In Nile University Final Exam Question 57: What is a key defining feature of open-source software development?
options: Collaborative development where source code is publicly available for inspection and modification
Software that is legally prohibited from being used for commercial purposes
Software that has no copyright licenses of any kind
Software written exclusively by university undergraduate students
questions.answer: Collaborative development where source code is publicly available for inspection and modification
questions.explanation: Open-source development is centered on transparency and collective peer review: source code is released under open licenses (e.g. MIT, Apache, GPL) that grant users the legal right to inspect, modify, and redistribute the software collaboratively.

why_wrong.Software that is legally prohibited from: Most open-source licenses explicitly permit commercial enterprise use.
Open source relies heavily on copyright law to enforce its licensing terms (copyleft or permissive).
why_wrong.Software written exclusively by universi: Global industry leaders (Linux, Python, React, PostgreSQL) are built by professional global communities.

questions.source: Nile University Final Exam Paper (Type B), Question 57

questions.question: In Nile University Final Exam Question 58: How do commercial open-source companies (such as Red Hat) primarily generate revenue?
options: Selling enterprise support, consulting, maintenance, and cloud services for the software product
Suing users who download the public source code
Selling proprietary compilers to decode the open source
Selling user private browser search histories
questions.answer: Selling enterprise support, consulting, maintenance, and cloud services for the software product
questions.explanation: Because open-source code is freely accessible, open-source business models monetize complementary services: enterprise technical support SLAs, security certification, customized integration, consulting, and managed cloud hosting.

why_wrong.Suing users who download the public sour: Open-source licenses explicitly grant the right to download and use the code.
Open source is compiled using standard public tools (e.g. GCC, Clang, OpenJDK).
why_wrong.Selling user private browser search hist: Unethical data-broker practice unrelated to open-source software business models.

marking_points: Monetizes support, maintenance, training, and managed services

questions.topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
questions.question: In a Scrum team developing a university portal, a faculty dean demands adding an emergency grading feature halfway through an active sprint. Who has the sole authority to accept this change and reorder the backlog?
options: The Product Owner, who owns the Product Backlog and balances business priorities with team capacity.
The Scrum Master, who dictates software features to developers.
Any individual developer working on the project.
The database administrator.
questions.answer: The Product Owner, who owns the Product Backlog and balances business priorities with team capacity.
questions.explanation: In Scrum governance, only the Product Owner has the authority to define user stories, prioritize the Product Backlog, and decide whether scope changes warrant modifying the current Sprint or queuing them for the next Sprint. The Scrum Master facilitates the process and removes blockers, but does not dictate business requirements.

why_wrong.The Scrum Master, who dictates software: Scrum Masters facilitate team health and process; they do not own business requirements.
Developers cannot accept arbitrary scope changes mid-sprint without Product Owner approval.
why_wrong.The database administrator: A technical role, not a project scope authority.

marking_points: Product Owner has sole authority over Product Backlog prioritization
questions.source: Software Engineering Concepts Lecture Notes, Section 5.4 & Scrum Guide

questions.topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
questions.question: Arrange the three phases of the Test-Driven Development (TDD) cycle in the correct operational sequence:
options: 1. RED (Write a unit test that defines a feature and watch it fail) -> 2. GREEN (Write the minimal production code necessary to pass the test) -> 3. REFACTOR (Clean up the code, eliminate duplication, and improve design while keeping tests green)
1. GREEN -> 2. RED -> 3. REFACTOR
1. REFACTOR -> 2. CODE -> 3. TEST
1. WRITE ALL CODE -> 2. MANUAL TEST -> 3. DEPLOY
questions.answer: 1. RED (Write a unit test that defines a feature and watch it fail) -> 2. GREEN (Write the minimal production code necessary to pass the test) -> 3. REFACTOR (Clean up the code, eliminate duplication, and improve design while keeping tests green)
questions.explanation: The foundational rhythm of TDD is Red-Green-Refactor: 1. Red: Confirm the test fails (validating that the test is actually checking something new); 2. Green: Write just enough code to satisfy the test; 3. Refactor: Improve internal design, remove duplication, and enhance readability while automated tests guarantee no regression.

why_wrong.1. GREEN -> 2. RED -> 3. REFACTOR: Writing code before tests violates the fundamental premise of TDD.
This is traditional ad-hoc development, the exact opposite of TDD.

questions.source: Software Engineering Concepts Lecture Notes, Section 9.6

questions.topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
questions.question: In a Kanban visual board, why are Work In Progress (WIP) limits enforced on workflow columns such as 'Code Review' or 'In Testing'?
options: To prevent multitasking and expose process bottlenecks, ensuring work items flow smoothly to completion rather than piling up half-finished.
To punish developers who finish their work early.
To prevent developers from working more than 2 hours a day.
To limit the total number of users allowed to access the website.
questions.answer: To prevent multitasking and expose process bottlenecks, ensuring work items flow smoothly to completion rather than piling up half-finished.
questions.explanation: Little's Law and Lean principles show that excessive work-in-progress increases cycle times and context-switching overhead. By capping the number of cards in an active column, if 'Code Review' hits its WIP limit, developers must help unblock pending reviews before starting new coding tasks ('Stop starting, start finishing').

why_wrong.To punish developers who finish work ear: Kanban fosters collaboration, not disciplinary penalties.
why_wrong.To limit developers to 2 hours a day: WIP limits govern task inventory, not working hours.
why_wrong.To limit website users: WIP limits apply to internal engineering tasks on the board, not web traffic.

questions.source: Software Engineering Process Models & Kanban Principles

questions.question: What are the three specific questions answered by development team members during the 15-minute Daily Scrum meeting?
options: 1. What did I accomplish yesterday? 2. What will I work on today? 3. Are there any impediments/blockers in my way?
1. How much bonus do I deserve? 2. Why is management wrong? 3. Who broke the build?
1. What language should we switch to? 2. When is lunch? 3. What bugs did QA find?
1. What is the database password? 2. Did the client pay? 3. What is my next promotion?
questions.answer: 1. What did I accomplish yesterday? 2. What will I work on today? 3. Are there any impediments/blockers in my way?
questions.explanation: The Daily Scrum is a brief, focused synchronization event where each team member answers: 1. What did I do yesterday that helped the team meet the Sprint Goal? 2. What will I do today? 3. What obstacles or blockers are impeding progress? Detailed architectural debates are deferred to separate follow-up sessions.

Daily standups are synchronization check-ins, not salary reviews.
Process distractions outside the scope of daily progress synchronization.

questions.topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
questions.question: What is the difference between Continuous Integration (CI) and Continuous Delivery (CD)?
questions.answer:
- CI: Automatically builds and tests code each time a developer commits to mainline.
- CD: Automatically prepares and validates software so it can be deployed to production at any time with a single click (or continuous deployment: deployed automatically).
questions.source: Software Engineering Concepts Lecture Notes, Section 5.6 & 9.7

questions.topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
questions.question: How does Kanban differ from Scrum?
questions.answer:
- Scrum uses fixed-length timeboxed Sprints (1-4 weeks), prescribed roles, and sprint backlogs.
- Kanban is a continuous-flow model with no fixed iterations, visualized on a board, with WIP limits constraining active tasks.
questions.explanation: Both are agile/lean, but differ in cadence and prescription.

case_studies.scenario: A healthtech startup in Abuja is transitioning from a traditional 12-month Waterfall cycle to Scrum to build an electronic telemedicine mobile application. The newly appointed Product Owner (a medical doctor) frequently visits developer desks during the middle of a 2-week Sprint, asking engineers to drop their current user stories to implement urgent new feature ideas she thought of that morning. As a result, the team has failed to deliver a working increment for three consecutive sprints.

sub_questions.topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
sub_questions.question: What Scrum rule is being violated, and how should the Scrum Master intervene to protect the team's commitment?
options: The Product Owner is violating Sprint stability: the Scrum Master must coach the Product Owner to place new feature requests onto the Product Backlog for prioritization in the NEXT sprint planning, leaving the current Sprint Goal intact.
The Scrum Master should immediately fire the developers for not complying with the doctor's wishes.
The team should abolish 2-week sprints and switch to daily deployments with zero planning.
The developers should work 20-hour overtime shifts to satisfy both the sprint backlog and the new requests.
sub_questions.answer: The Product Owner is violating Sprint stability: the Scrum Master must coach the Product Owner to place new feature requests onto the Product Backlog for prioritization in the NEXT sprint planning, leaving the current Sprint Goal intact.
sub_questions.explanation: A core premise of Scrum is that once a Sprint begins, the Sprint Goal is protected against mid-sprint scope churn that endangers completion. If an idea is truly critical, the Product Owner adds it to the top of the Product Backlog for the upcoming Sprint. Only in extraordinary circumstances where the Sprint Goal becomes completely obsolete may the Product Owner formally cancel the entire Sprint.

why_wrong.The Scrum Master should fire the develop: The developers are properly defending their agreed sprint commitment.
Abandoning process structure creates total chaos.
why_wrong.The developers should work 20-hour overt: Violates the Agile principle of sustainable development pace.

marking_points: Identifies violation of Sprint commitment and scope stability
Directs new items to Product Backlog for next sprint planning
sub_questions.source: Scrum Implementation Case Study & Agile Manifesto

sub_questions.topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
sub_questions.question: To prevent future sprint delivery failures, define what a formal 'Definition of Done' (DoD) should include for each user story before it can be demonstrated at the Sprint Review.
sub_questions.answer:
A robust Definition of Done (DoD) must require:
1. Code Implementation & Review: All production code written, reviewed via peer pull request, and conforming to coding standards.
2. Automated Testing: Unit tests and integration tests passing with zero failures, meeting minimum code coverage (e.g. >= 80%).
3. Acceptance Criteria Satisfied: Feature fulfills all specific business acceptance criteria defined in the user story.
4. Documentation & Integration: API endpoints documented, code merged to the development branch via CI pipeline, and deployed to a staging environment ready for stakeholder demonstration.
sub_questions.explanation: The Definition of Done ensures high quality and prevents half-finished work from being claimed as complete.
marking_points: Code reviewed and adhering to standards
Automated tests passing with adequate coverage
Integrated into mainline via CI and deployed to staging
sub_questions.source: Scrum Quality Standards & Definition of Done

case_studies.scenario: A software agency in Lagos is building an automated algorithmic trading engine. The financial stakes are extremely high: a single decimal point calculation error could lose millions of Naira within seconds. The chief engineer mandates Pair Programming and strict Test-Driven Development (TDD). The chief financial officer objects, arguing that having two developers work on one computer cuts programming productivity in half and wastes 50% of developer salaries.

sub_questions.topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
sub_questions.question: How does empirical software engineering research rebut the CFO's argument regarding the economics of Pair Programming in high-stakes systems?
options: Pair programming incurs only ~15% additional development time while reducing defect density by 15-50%, drastically reducing post-release bug fixing costs which are 10-100x more expensive in production.
Pair programming actually produces 400% more lines of code per hour.
The CFO is right; pair programming is only used when an office runs out of computers.
Pair programming eliminates the need to compile code.
sub_questions.answer: Pair programming incurs only ~15% additional development time while reducing defect density by 15-50%, drastically reducing post-release bug fixing costs which are 10-100x more expensive in production.
sub_questions.explanation: Empirical studies (e.g. Cockburn & Williams) demonstrate that pairing increases effort by approximately 15%, but generates significantly cleaner code with 15–50% fewer defects. Because fixing defects in live trading engines costs 10 to 100 times more than catching them during coding (Boehm's cost of change), pair programming yields massive net economic savings.

why_wrong.Pair programming produces 400% more code: Pairing produces more concise, less bloated code, not more raw volume.
why_wrong.The CFO is right; only used when running: Pairing is an intentional quality discipline, not a hardware shortage workaround.

marking_points: Contrasts with 10-100x production defect remediation cost
sub_questions.source: Software Engineering Economics & Pair Programming Studies

sub_questions.topic: Agile Software Development, Scrum, Kanban, XP & DevOps
sub_questions.question: Explain why Test-Driven Development (TDD) provides a crucial safety net for continuous refactoring in high-stakes financial trading algorithms.
sub_questions.answer:
1. Comprehensive Regression Safety: Because every feature starts with an automated test before code is written, a comprehensive suite of unit tests covers all business logic. When engineers refactor trading algorithms for speed or readability, running the test suite immediately confirms that no existing calculations or boundary conditions were broken.
2. Modular, Testable Design: TDD forces developers to write small, decoupled, highly cohesive functions that can be instantiated and verified in isolation, preventing the emergence of tangled spaghetti code.
3. Living Specification: The test suite serves as an unambiguous, executable specification documenting exact mathematical inputs and expected trade outcomes under edge conditions.
sub_questions.explanation: TDD eliminates the fear of refactoring by providing instantaneous automated verification.
marking_points: Comprehensive regression testing safety net during refactoring
Forces modular, decoupled, testable architectural design
Acts as executable living documentation of business rules
